title: Pointwise diagonal Kummer model with inertia-preserving etale neighbourhood
statement:
Let $(X,M)$ be a separated locally Noetherian fs log regular scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-weil-proper-morphism] with an action of a finite group $G$ by log automorphisms [def-per-fs-log-group-action]. Let $\bar x$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], put $H=\operatorname{Stab}_G(\bar x)$ and $n=|H|$, and assume the action is very tame at $\bar x$ in the pointwise sense of [def-per-very-tame-fs-log-action]. There exist an affine fs log scheme $W$, a geometric point $\bar w$ of $W$, an $H$-action on $W$, and a strict $H$-equivariant etale morphism $v:W\to X$ with $v\bar w=\bar x$, where $H$ acts on $X$ by its inclusion in $G$. For every geometric point $\bar z$ of $W$ the inclusion induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{Stab}_H(\bar z)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Stab}_G(v\bar z)$. There are a primitive $n$th root of unity $\zeta_n$, the ring $\Lambda=\mathbf Z[\zeta_n,1/n]$, a Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebra $B$, sharp fs monoids $P\subseteq Q$, and a pairing $\chi:H_{\rm ab}\otimes_{\mathbf Z}Q^{\rm gp}\to\langle\zeta_n\rangle$ such that $P=\{q\in Q:\chi_h(q)=1\text{ for every }h\in H\}$, every element of $Q$ has a positive multiple in $P$, and $Q^{\rm gp}/P^{\rm gp}$ is annihilated by $n$. Here $H_{\rm ab}$ is the quotient by commutators, sharp means that $0$ is the only unit, and $\langle\zeta_n\rangle\subset\Lambda^\times$ is the cyclic group generated by $\zeta_n$. A chart $P\to B$ and an $H$-equivariant isomorphism of log schemes identify
$$W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(B\otimes_{\Lambda[P]}\Lambda[Q]\bigr),\qquad h(b\otimes z^q)=b\otimes\chi_h(q)z^q.$$
The log structure on this spectrum is the one with chart $Q$, the action fixes $B$, and the chart $Q$ identifies with the characteristic monoid at $\bar w$. The monoid algebra $\Lambda[C]$ is free over $\Lambda$ on symbols $z^c$, with $z^cz^{c'}=z^{c+c'}$. Strict and etale mean [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation, def-weil-etale-morphism]. The pairing need not be faithful: no generic freeness of the $G$-action is assumed.

source.place: VI Proposition 3.5(a)--(c), proof 3.7(a)--(c), printed pp.74--76; local standard-cover presentation VI 2.2--2.3, pp.72--73. Inertia-preserving shrinking for the separated scheme setting: VIII 5.3.6 and proof of 5.3.7, pp.124--125. The action is allowed to have a kernel.

proof.text: By [lem-per-very-tame-equivariant-sharp-chart], the invertibility of $n=|H|$ and triviality on the characteristic give an $H$-equivariant pointed etale neighbourhood with sharp chart $a:Q\to M$, diagonal pairing $\chi$, and fixed primitive $n$th root of unity. Apply [lem-per-affine-inert-equivariant-refinement] to this neighbourhood, taking the prescribed invariant open where $n$ is invertible. Denote the resulting affine neighbourhood by $U=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$, with point $\bar u$, and pull back the log structure and chart. Its map to $X$ is strict and preserves the full $G$-inertia at every geometric point. Etale strict-local invariance [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] identifies its strict local log stalk at $\bar u$ with that at $\bar x$; thus the very-tame conditions at this point hold, and $Q$ still identifies with the characteristic. The same invariance at all points makes $U$ log regular. The roots and chart define the $H$-fixed coefficient map $\Lambda=\mathbf Z[\zeta_n,1/n]\to R_0$.

The order of every subgroup of $H$ is invertible on $U$, since its order divides the unit $n$. Apply [lem-per-tame-admissible-scheme-quotient] to the affine Noetherian scheme $U$: its whole affine open is invariant. It gives the finite quotient $U\to Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$, where $B_0=R_0^H$ is Noetherian and the geometric fibres are the $H$-orbits. Let $\bar y$ be the image of $\bar u$, and put $A=\mathcal O_{U,\bar u}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Y_0,\bar y}$. By [lem-per-finite-quotient-strict-local-invariants], $B=A^H$, $A$ is finite over $B$, and the invariant log stalk is $M_{\bar u}^H$. Both strict local rings are Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]. No generic freeness is needed for either cited quotient assertion.

Write $I=(a(q):0\ne q\in Q)A$. Very tameness at $\bar u$ says that $H$ is trivial on $A/I$. Apply [lem-per-very-tame-local-kummer-quotient] to $A,H,Q,a,\chi$ and the finite inclusion $B=A^H\subset A$. It gives the sharp fs monoid $P=Q\cap L$, with $L=\{t\in Q^{\rm gp}:\chi_h(t)=1\ (h\in H)\}$, $P^{\rm gp}=L\supseteq nQ^{\rm gp}$, and the invariant chart $b:P\to B$ at the closed point. It also gives $B/J\simeq A/I$, for $J=(a(p):0\ne p\in P)B$. Globally $a(p)\in R_0$ is $H$-fixed for $p\in P$, so the same formula defines $P\to B_0$. Further, $nq\in P$ for every $q\in Q$, since $\chi_h(nq)=\chi_h(q)^n=1$.

source.place: VI 3.7(b), invariant monoid and chart, pp.75--76.

proof.text:
The integral injection $B\hookrightarrow A$ has equal Krull dimensions by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal]. Because $nQ^{\rm gp}\subseteq P^{\rm gp}\subseteq Q^{\rm gp}$, the rational ranks of the two groups agree. Log regularity at $\bar u$ and the stratum isomorphism therefore give
$$\dim B=\dim A=\dim(A/I)+\operatorname{rank}Q^{\rm gp}=\dim(B/J)+\operatorname{rank}P^{\rm gp},$$
and $B/J$ is regular. The chart $P$ identifies with the characteristic at the closed point, so $J$ is its nonunit ideal. Endow $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with this chart log structure. It is log regular at the closed point by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and everywhere by [lem-per-log-regular-generization], since every prime of a local ring is a generization of its maximal ideal. This uses generization, without assuming an open log regular locus.

Set $C_0=B_0\otimes_{\Lambda[P]}\Lambda[Q]$ and $C=B\otimes_{B_0}C_0$. For generators $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ of $Q$, the monomials $z^{\sum r_iq_i}$ with $0\le r_i<n$ generate each of these algebras as a module over its coefficient ring: move every multiple $nq_i\in P$ into the coefficients. Hence both algebras are finite, and are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. In the closed fibre of $C/B$, each nonzero monomial is nilpotent, as $(z^q)^n=b(nq)$ is zero there; $nq\ne0$, since sharp saturated monoids have torsion-free group completion (if $nt=0$, saturation puts both $t$ and $-t$ in $Q$, so $t$ is a unit and is zero). The ideal generated by the finitely many nonzero monomial generators is nilpotent, and its quotient is $k(B)$. The finite henselian-product theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product] now shows that $C$ is a single henselian local ring with residue field $k(B)$. Thus $C$ is strictly henselian, and its chart $Q$ is sharp at the closed point.

source.place: VI 2.2--2.3, pp.72--73; the standard-cover ring of VI 3.7(b)--(c), pp.75--76.

proof.text: The morphism $(\operatorname{Spec}C,Q)\to(\operatorname{Spec}B,P)$ is exactly the standard chart base change: $P\subset Q$ is injective, Kummer, and its finite group cokernel is killed by the unit $n$; its chart comparison is the identity. Thus [lem-per-invertible-kummer-chart-log-regular], applied to the log regular base of Step 4, makes $\operatorname{Spec}C$ log regular. It is locally Noetherian by Step 5. By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure], every local ring of this log scheme is a normal domain. As $C$ is local, $C$ itself is a domain.

source.place: VI 1.8, p.70, and VI 3.7(c), p.76; normality as in VIII 3.5, pp.114--115.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-tame-diagonal-standard-closed-immersion] to the finite quotient of Step 2, using the diagonal chart and trivial-stratum condition of Step 3. Its strict-local clause says that the natural comparison $C\to A$, $b\otimes z^q\mapsto b\,a(q)$, is surjective; including the common coefficient ring $\Lambda$ instead of $\mathbf Z$ gives the same tensor algebra. The composite $B\to C\to A$ is the injective invariant inclusion, so $B\to C$ is injective. Finiteness and the integral-dimension lemmas give $\dim C=\dim B=\dim A$. These dimensions are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension]. The surjection has zero kernel: a nonzero kernel in the domain $C$ would make every prime containing it nonzero. A prime chain of maximal length in $A$ would lift to a chain in $C$ that extends by $(0)$ at the bottom, contradicting equal finite dimensions. Therefore $C\simeq A$.

source.place: VI 3.7(b)--(c), closed immersion (3.c) and its upgrade to an isomorphism, p.76.

proof.text: Consider the global $B_0$-linear comparison $F:C_0\to R_0$, given by $b\otimes z^q\mapsto b\,a(q)$. The geometric fibre of $U\to Y_0$ at $\bar y$ is a single point: it is an $H$-orbit and $\bar u$ is fixed by all of $H$. By [lem-trf-finite-base-strict-localization] the base change of $U$ to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is therefore its single strict localization $\operatorname{Spec}A$, rather than a product with additional factors. Consequently $R_0\otimes_{B_0}B\simeq A$, canonically with its action and monomial maps, and $F\otimes B$ is precisely the isomorphism $C\to A$ of Step 7.

source.place: VI 3.5(b)--(c), etale-local versus strict-local formulations, pp.74--76.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p\subset B_0$ be the point under $\bar y$. Localization of modules is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so the kernel and cokernel of $F_{\mathfrak p}$ are the localizations of those of $F$. The map $(B_0)_{\mathfrak p}\to B$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]. Flat tensor exactness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] identifies the base changes of the kernel and cokernel of $F_{\mathfrak p}$ with zero, since Step 8 makes its base change an isomorphism. Faithful-flat detection of zero modules [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-tensor-zero] gives $\ker F_{\mathfrak p}=\operatorname{coker}F_{\mathfrak p}=0$. Both $\ker F$ and $\operatorname{coker}F$ are finite $B_0$-modules: $C_0$ and $R_0$ are finite, the cokernel is generated by the images of generators, and the kernel is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. For each of their finitely many generators, vanishing at $\mathfrak p$ gives a denominator outside $\mathfrak p$ killing it. The product $f\in B_0\setminus\mathfrak p$ of these denominators kills all the generators after localization. Thus $F_f:(C_0)_f\xrightarrow{\sim}(R_0)_f$ is an isomorphism. This localization is on the invariant base, so the whole standard tensor model is retained.

source.place: VI 3.5(b)--(c), pp.74--76, finite-module descent of the strict-local comparison; Stacks Tags 00HP (algebra-lemma-ff), 00IK (algebra-lemma-Noetherian-basic).

proof.text: Take the algebra called $B$ in the item to be $(B_0)_f$ (the strictly local ring denoted $B$ in Steps 2--9 was only an intermediate object), and take $W=\operatorname{Spec}(R_0)_f$. This coefficient algebra is Noetherian, since it is the coordinate ring of the affine open $D(f)$ in the Noetherian scheme $Y_0$ [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Step 9 identifies $W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{\Lambda[P]}\Lambda[Q])$. The comparison sends $z^q$ to $a(q)$, so the log structures on both sides are the associated chart $Q$; it is therefore an isomorphism of log schemes. The map is $H$-equivariant because $H$ fixes $B$ and sends $a(q)$ to $\chi_h(q)a(q)$. The point $\bar u$ lies in $W$ because $f\notin\mathfrak p$. Restricting the original strict etale map gives $v:W\to X$; its geometric stabilizers still equal the full $G$-stabilizers, since this was true throughout $U$ and $f$ is invariant. The characteristic at the selected point remains $Q$. The description of $P$, the Kummer multiples and the annihilation by $n$ are Step 3. None of the construction identifies $H$ with a faithful character group, so actions with a kernel are included.

proof_origin.place: VI 3.7(a)--(c), pp.75--76, with explicit generic affine inert refinement, generization, finite-module descent and the nonfaithful-action case.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q41-4f9077a00 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 10 steps, the two new nodes and every cited statement in full, and checked the source in ILO: VI 1.2-1.3 (p.69; generization of log regularity is stated there, citing Kato 1994 7.1), VI 3.1 and 3.4-3.7 (pp.73-76), VIII 5.3.6-5.3.7 (pp.124-125) and VI 4.1. Steps 1-3 meet every hypothesis of the sharp-chart, tame-quotient, strict-local-invariants and local-Kummer-quotient nodes. Pointwise very tameness supplies these, and the order n is invertible on the affine refinement. Step 4: dim B = dim A, the two monoid ranks agree because nQ^gp lies in P^gp, and B/J = A/I, so Spec B is log regular at the closed point and, by generization, everywhere. Step 5: C is finite (monomials with exponents below n generate it), the nonzero monomials are nilpotent in the closed fibre because Q^gp is torsion-free, so C is strictly henselian. Step 6: Kummer ascent makes Spec C log regular, so C is a normal domain. Step 7: the strict-local surjection C -> A between domains of equal finite dimension has zero kernel (this is the content of VI 3.7(c)). Steps 8-9: the geometric fibre over the fixed point is one point, and faithfully flat descent of the finite kernel and cokernel gives an isomorphism over an invariant principal open of the base. Step 10 covers every clause of the item, including actions with a kernel. New nodes: lem-per-affine-inert-equivariant-refinement is true (translate product, closed fixed loci X^g, open-and-closed fixed loci over X^h, norms; tested on Z/2 acting on A^1). lem-per-log-regular-generization is true (ILO VI 1.3). Neither duplicates an existing node or restates the item, and there is no cycle. Batch 5: the cited trf nodes (fs-log definition, finite-base strict localization, ind-etale strict-local invariance, Niziol 2.6 divisorial structure, Noetherian submodule) are general results. Their closures contain no thm-trf, nt-assume or Poincare node, so these flags are generic. Artin-Gabber route check: lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve does not use this item. The item is reached only through the sfb chain (gabber-global-snc-alteration -> gabber-absolute-equivariant-modification -> abelian-inert-rigidification-cover -> very-tame-locus-open).
